Circa un’ora dopo, non tornò più fino a [[motifs/noon|mattina]], quando.

Portò ad Augusto una grande quantità di carne scadente e budino.

Quando siamo rimasti [[Alone|soli]], ho partecipato con entusiasmo, senza esitazioni.

Tornando attraverso il buco… Nessun altro scese laggiù.

Durante il giorno stavo nel castello di prua; di [[motifs/night|notte]], mi recavo nella stanza di Augustus.

Letto dove dormii profondamente e serenamente fino quasi all’alba.

Quando mi svegliò sentendo del trambusto sul ponte, e io ripresi i sensi…

Il mio rifugio… il più in fretta possibile. Quando il giorno fu completamente…

"Broke... ma abbiamo scoperto che Tiger aveva quasi ripreso le forze."

Del tutto… e senza mostrare alcun segno di idrofobia, beveva…

Quel pochissimo [[motifs/water|acqua]] che gli fu offerto con grande apparente entusiasmo.

Durante il giorno riprese tutto il suo precedente vigore e appetito.

Il suo strano comportamento, senza alcun [[concepts/doubt|dubbio]], era causato da.

Qualità dannosa dell’aria nel ponte di carico… e nessuna connessione con nulla.

Con una follia canina. Non riuscivo a gioire abbastanza del fatto che avessi.

Continuò a portarlo con sé fin dal momento in cui lo aveva preso dalla scatola. Quel giorno…

Trentesimo giugno, e il tredicesimo da quando il Grampus ha levato l’ancora

Di Nantucket.



Il 2 luglio, come al solito, il compagno di bordo arrivò sottocoperta ubriaco… e…

Un umore eccessivamente allegro. Si avvicinò alla cabina di Augustus e…

Dandogli una pacca sulla schiena, gli chiese se pensasse di riuscirci.

Comportarsi bene se gli venisse permesso di farlo… e se sarebbe disposto a prometterlo.

Non intendo più entrare nella cabina… Certo, riguardo a questo…

Il compagno rispose affermativamente, quando il delinquente lo costrinse…

Libertà… dopo averlo fatto bere da una fiaschetta di rum che aveva tirato fuori…

Dalla tasca del suo cappotto… Entrambi salirono sul ponte, e io non li vidi più.

Per circa tre ore… Poi tornò giù con il “buono”.

Titolo:  
La notizia che aveva ottenuto il permesso di muoversi liberamente sul brigantino…

Felice ovunque, davanti al albero maestro… e che fosse stato…

Gli fu ordinato di [[motifs/sleep|dormire]], come al solito, nella cabina di prua. Mi portò con sé.

Anche un buon pasto e una abbondante quantità di [[motifs/water|acqua]]. La brigata.

Ancora alla ricerca della nave proveniente dalle Isole di Capo Verde… e una vela era visibile.

Ora è in vista; si pensava che fosse proprio quella di cui si parlava. Mentre…

Gli eventi dei successivi otto giorni ebbero scarso rilievo…

Non aveva alcuna relazione diretta con gli eventi principali della mia narrazione.

Titolo:  
Li presenterò qui sotto forma di diario, poiché non desidero altro.

Ometterli del tutto.



3 luglio: Augusto mi fornì tre coperte, con cui…

Creai un comodo letto nel mio nascondiglio… Nessuno venne.

Sotto il sole, tranne che per la mia compagna… Durante il giorno, Tiger se ne andava da solo.

Posizionato nella cuccetta proprio accanto all’apertura, dormì profondamente…

Se non si è ancora completamente ripresi dagli effetti della sua malattia.

Verso la [[motifs/night|notte]], un improvviso colpo di [[motifs/wind|vento]] colpì la brigata prima che fosse possibile levare l’ancora.

Raffiche violente… e per poco non la capovolgono. La tempesta si placa.

Tuttavia, immediatamente, e non si verificò alcun danno oltre alla semplice rottura.

Titolo:  
Del trinchetto… Per tutto il giorno, Dirk Peters trattò Augustus in quel modo.

Con grande gentilezza, iniziò una lunga conversazione con lui.

Riguardo all'Oceano Pacifico e alle isole che aveva visitato…

In quella regione… Gli chiese se non volesse andare con lui.

I ammutinanti in un viaggio esplorativo e di piacere...

Quarti… e disse che gli uomini stavano gradualmente prendendo posizione da quella parte.

“Le opinioni del mio compagno… A questo, Augusto ritenne fosse meglio rispondere che…”

Sarei felice di partecipare a un’avventura del genere, visto che non c’è nulla di meglio.

Potrebbe essere fatto… e che qualsiasi cosa sia preferibile a un comportamento piratesco.

La vita.



4 luglio: La nave visibile si rivelò essere una piccola brigantina…

Liverpool, e poté proseguire indisturbato. Augusto trascorse…

La maggior parte del suo [[motifs/time|tempo]] la trascorreva sul ponte, con l’obiettivo di ottenere tutto ciò che gli serviva.

Informazioni a sua disposizione riguardo alle intenzioni di…

I ribelli… Avevano spesso litigi violenti tra loro.

Get Lost in Their Own World

Overboard… La festa del marinaio prendeva piede… Jim Bonner

Apparteneva alla banda del cuoco, di cui Peters era un sostenitore.



5 luglio. All’alba iniziò a soffiare una brezza forte proveniente da…



<span class="atom-split" data-atom="chapter_06--part_04" data-title="The Narrative of A. Gordon Pym (Raven Edition) — Chapter 6 (part 4)" data-chapter="Chapter 06" data-kind="excerpt" data-tags="motif/noon,motif/ship,motif/water,motif/wind,setting/ship,character/jones,character/richard"></span>


west, which at [[motifs/noon|noon]] freshened into a gale, so that the brig could

carry nothing more than her trysail and foresail. In taking in

the foretopsail, Simms, one of the common hands, and belonging

also to the cook’s gang, fell overboard, being very much in

liquor, and was drowned—no attempt being made to save him. The

whole number of persons on board was now thirteen, to wit: Dirk

Peters; Seymour, the black cook; [[characters/jones|Jones]], Greely, Hartman Rogers

and William Allen, all of the cook’s party; the mate, whose name

I never learned; Absalom Hicks, Wilson, John Hunty [[characters/richard|Richard]]

Parker, of the mate’s party;—besides Augustus and myself.



July 6th. The gale lasted all this day, blowing in heavy squalls,

accompanied with rain. The brig took in a good deal of [[motifs/water|water]]

through her seams, and one of the pumps was kept continually

going, Augustus being forced to take his turn. Just at twilight a

large [[motifs/ship|ship]] passed close by us, without having been discovered

until within hail. The [[motifs/ship|ship]] was supposed to be the one for which

the mutineers were on the lookout. The mate hailed her, but the

reply was drowned in the roaring of the gale. At eleven, a sea

was shipped amidships, which tore away a great portion of the

larboard bulwarks, and did some other slight damage. Toward

morning the weather moderated, and at sunrise there was very

little [[motifs/wind|wind]].



July 7th. There was a heavy swell running all this day, during

which the brig, being light, rolled excessively, and many

articles broke loose in the hold, as I could hear distinctly from

my hiding-place. I suffered a great deal from sea-sickness.

Peters had a long conversation this day with Augustus, and told

him that two of his gang, Greely and Allen, had gone over to the

mate, and were resolved to turn pirates. He put several questions

to Augustus which he did not then exactly understand. During a

part of this evening the leak gained upon the vessel; and little

could be done to remedy it, as it was occasioned by the brig's

straining, and taking in the [[motifs/water|water]] through her seams. A sail was

thrummed, and got under the bows, which aided us in some measure,

so that we began to gain upon the leak.



July 8th. A light breeze sprang up at sunrise from the eastward,

when the mate headed the brig to the southwest, with the

intention of making some of the West India islands in pursuance

of his piratical designs. No opposition was made by Peters or the

cook—at least none in the hearing of Augustus. All idea of taking

the vessel from the Cape Verds was abandoned. The leak was now

easily kept under by one pump going every three quarters of an

hour. The sail was drawn from beneath the bows. Spoke two small

schooners during the day.



July 9th. Fine weather. All hands employed in repairing bulwarks.

Peters had again a long conversation with Augustus, and spoke

more plainly than he had done heretofore. He said nothing should

induce him to come into the mate’s views, and even hinted his

intention of taking the brig out of his hands. He asked my friend

if he could depend upon his aid in such case, to which Augustus

said, “Yes,” without hesitation. Peters then said he would sound

the others of his party upon the subject, and went away. During

the remainder of the day Augustus had no opportunity of speaking

with him privately.


<span class="qlang-split" data-lang="it"></span>

Ovest, che alle [[motifs/noon|mattine]] si trasformò in una tempesta violenta, tanto da rendere impossibile per la brigata.

Titolo:  
“Con soltanto la vela di mezzana e la vela di prua…”.

Il trinchetto, Simms, uno dei marinai comuni… e appartenente…

Anche il gruppo di cuochi finì in acqua, essendo tutti molto impegnati…

Alcol… e fu annegato: nessuno tentò di salvarlo.

Il numero totale di persone a bordo era ora tredici, e precisamente: Dirk.

Peters; Seymour, il cuoco nero; [[characters/jones|Jones]], Greely, Hartman Rogers.

E William Allen, tutti membri dell’equipaggio della cucina; il secondo ufficiale, il cui nome…

Non l’ho mai imparato; Absalom Hicks, Wilson, John Hunty [[characters/richard|Richard]]

Parker, che faceva parte del gruppo di amici del marinaio; oltre ad Augustus e a me.



6 luglio: La tempesta è durata tutto il giorno, con forti raffiche di vento.

Ampio accompagnato dalla pioggia, il brigantino assorbì una grande quantità di [[motifs/water|acqua]].

“Attraverso tutte le sue fessure… e uno dei tacchi veniva continuamente tenuto fermo.”

“Going… Augustus viene costretto a prendere il suo turno. Proprio al crepuscolo…”

Una grande [[motifs/ship|nave]] ci è passata vicino senza essere scoperta.

Fino a distanze ravvicinate. Quella[[motifs/ship|nave]] avrebbe dovuto essere proprio quella per cui.

“I mutinieri erano all’erta… Il secondo ufficiale la chiamò, ma…”

La risposta fu sommersa dal fragore della tempesta. Alle undici, il mare…

Il titolo è stato posizionato nella parte centrale della nave, il che ha causato la distruzione di una grande parte di essa.

“Parapetti di babordo e altri lievi danni… Verso…”

La mattina seguente il tempo si rasserenò, e al sorgere del sole…

Un debole [[motifs/wind|vento]].



7 luglio. Per tutto il giorno c’era un forte mareggio in corso…

Il brigantino, essendo leggero, rollava eccessivamente; molti…

Articoli che si liberarono nel ponte di stiva… ne sentivo chiaramente il rumore

Il mio nascondiglio. Ho sofferto molto a causa del mal di mare.

Peters ebbe una lunga conversazione quel giorno con Augustus e gli raccontò…

Quello a cui due membri della sua banda, Greely e Allen, erano passati dall’altra parte…

Amici, decisero di diventare pirati… Lui pose diverse domande.

“#A Augusto, che all’epoca non capì del tutto il significato.”

Durante questa serata, la perdita d’acqua ha peggiorato sulla nave… e poco altro si può dire.

Titolo:  
Si potrebbero adottare misure per rimediare, poiché la situazione è scaturita dalle caratteristiche particolari della brigata in questione.

Si sforzava, assorbendo l’[[motifs/water|acqua]] attraverso le fessure. Una vela.

“Rimbombava forte, e si insinuò sotto le vele, il che ci aiutò in qualche modo.”

Così iniziammo a ridurre il ritardo causato dalla perdita.



8 luglio: Al sorgere del sole, una leggera brezza soffiò da est.

Quando il capitano guidò la brig verso sud-ovest…

Titolo:  
L’intenzione di rendere alcune isole delle Indie Occidentali…

Titolo:  
Dei suoi perversi progetti… Nessuna opposizione da parte di Peters o degli altri.

Nessuno che cucini, almeno non secondo quanto riferito da Augusto… Qualsiasi pensiero riguardante la preparazione di cibo è del tutto assente.

Il velivolo proveniente dalle Isole di Capo Verde fu abbandonato; la perdita d’acqua continuava…

Facilmente mantenibile con un solo pompaggio ogni tre quarti d’ora

Ore… La vela fu ritirata sotto la prua; due piccoli…

Durante il giorno, erano schooner.



9 luglio. Tempo bello. Tutti impegnati nella riparazione dei parapetti.

Peters ebbe di nuovo una lunga conversazione con Augustus e parlò…

Più chiaramente di quanto avesse fatto fino ad allora… Disse che nulla doveva essere lasciato all’indeterminato.

Indurlo ad aderire al punto di vista del compagno, e persino gli fece intendere…

Titolo:  
L’intenzione di strappargli la nave dalle mani… Chiese a mio amico…

Se potesse contare sul suo aiuto in una situazione del genere, a quale scopo Augusto…

Disse: “Sì”, senza esitazione. Poi Peters aggiunse che avrebbe fatto ciò che era necessario.

Gli altri membri del suo gruppo discussero dell’argomento e poi se ne andarono. Nel frattempo…

Il resto della giornata, Augustus non ebbe l’opportunità di parlare.

In privato, con lui.



<span class="atom-split" data-atom="chapter_07--part_01" data-title="The Narrative of A. Gordon Pym (Raven Edition) — Chapter 7 (part 1)" data-chapter="Chapter 07" data-kind="excerpt" data-tags="motif/night,motif/time,motif/water,motif/well,motif/wind,concept/fear,character/jones"></span>


CHAPTER 7





July 10. Spoke a brig from Rio, bound to Norfolk. Weather hazy,

with a light baffling [[motifs/wind|wind]] from the eastward. To-day Hartman

Rogers died, having been attacked on the eighth with spasms after

drinking a glass of grog. This man was of the cook’s party, and

one upon whom Peters placed his main reliance. He told Augustus

that he believed the mate had poisoned him, and that he expected,

if he did not be on the look-out, his own turn would come

shortly. There were now only himself, [[characters/jones|Jones]], and the cook

belonging to his own gang—on the other side there were five. He

had spoken to [[characters/jones|Jones]] about taking the command from the mate; but

the project having been coolly received, he had been deterred

from pressing the matter any further, or from saying any thing to

the cook. It was [[motifs/well|well]], as it happened, that he was so prudent,

for in the afternoon the cook expressed his determination of

siding with the mate, and went over formally to that party; while

[[characters/jones|Jones]] took an opportunity of quarrelling with Peters, and hinted

that he would let the mate know of the plan in agitation. There

was now, evidently, no [[motifs/time|time]] to be lost, and Peters expressed his

determination of attempting to take the vessel at all hazards,

provided Augustus would lend him his aid. My friend at once

assured him of his willingness to enter into any plan for that

purpose, and, thinking the opportunity a favourable one, made

known the fact of my being on board. At this the hybrid was not

more astonished than delighted, as he had no reliance whatever

upon [[characters/jones|Jones]], whom he already considered as belonging to the party

of the mate. They went below immediately, when Augustus called to

me by name, and Peters and myself were soon made acquainted. It

was agreed that we should attempt to retake the vessel upon the

first good opportunity, leaving [[characters/jones|Jones]] altogether out of our

councils. In the event of [[success]], we were to run the brig into

the first port that offered, and deliver her up. The desertion of

his party had frustrated Peters’ design of going into the

Pacific—an adventure which could not be accomplished without a

crew, and he depended upon either getting acquitted upon trial,

on the score of insanity (which he solemnly avowed had actuated

him in lending his aid to the mutiny), or upon obtaining a

pardon, if found guilty, through the representations of Augustus

and myself. Our deliberations were interrupted for the present by

the cry of, “All hands take in sail,” and Peters and Augustus ran

up on deck.



As usual, the crew were nearly all drunk; and, before sail could

be properly taken in, a violent squall laid the brig on her

beam-ends. By keeping her away, however, she righted, having

shipped a good deal of [[motifs/water|water]]. Scarcely was everything secure,

when another squall took the vessel, and immediately afterward

another—no damage being done. There was every appearance of a

gale of [[motifs/wind|wind]], which, indeed, shortly came on, with great fury,

from the northward and westward. All was made as snug as

possible, and we laid-to, as usual, under a close-reefed

foresail. As [[motifs/night|night]] drew on, the [[motifs/wind|wind]] increased in violence, with

a remarkably heavy sea. Peters now came into the forecastle with

Augustus, and we resumed our deliberations.



We agreed that no opportunity could be more favourable than the

present for carrying our designs into effect, as an attempt at

such a moment would never be anticipated. As the brig was snugly

laid-to, there would be no necessity of manoeuvring her until

good weather, when, if we succeeded in our attempt, we might

liberate one, or perhaps two of the men, to aid us in taking her

into port. The main difficulty was the great disproportion in our

forces. There were only three of us, and in the cabin there were

nine. All the arms on board, too, were in their possession, with

the exception of a pair of small pistols which Peters had

concealed about his person, and the large seaman’s knife which he

always wore in the waistband of his pantaloons. From certain

indications, too—such, for example, as there being no such thing

as an axe or a handspike lying in their customary places—we began

to [[concepts/fear|fear]] that the mate had his suspicions, at least in regard to

Peters, and that he would let slip no opportunity of getting rid

of him. It was clear, indeed, that what we should determine to do

could not be done too soon. Still the odds were too much against

us to allow of our proceeding without the greatest caution.



Peters proposed that he should go up on deck, and enter into

conversation with the watch (Allen), when he would be able to

throw him into the sea without trouble, and without making any

disturbance, by seizing a good opportunity, that Augustus and

myself should then come up, and endeavour to provide ourselves

with some kind of weapons from the deck, and that we should then

make a rush together, and secure the companion-way before any

opposition could be offered. I objected to this, because I could

not believe that the mate (who was a cunning fellow in all

matters which did not affect his superstitious prejudices) would

suffer himself to be so easily entrapped. The very fact of there

being a watch on deck at all was sufficient proof that he was

upon the alert,—it not being usual except in vessels where

discipline is most rigidly enforced, to station a watch on deck


<span class="qlang-split" data-lang="it"></span>

CAPITOLO 7





10 luglio: Ho parlato con un brigantino proveniente da Rio, diretto a Norfolk. Il tempo era nebbioso.

Con una leggera brezza sorprendente che soffiava da est. Oggi, Hartman.

Rogers morì dopo essere stato attaccato l’ottavo giorno; subì convulsioni in seguito all’aggressione.

Bevendo un bicchiere di grog… Quest’uomo faceva parte del gruppo dei cuochi.

Colui su cui Peters contava soprattutto… Glielo disse ad Augustus.

Titolo:  
Credeva che il compagno di viaggio lo avesse avvelenato, e si aspettava…

Se non fosse stato attento, sarebbe arrivato il suo turno.

Poco dopo. Ora c'erano soltanto lui, [[characters/jones|Jones]] e il cuoco.

Apparteneva alla sua stessa banda… mentre dall’altra parte ce n’erano cinque. Lui…

Aveva parlato con [[characters/jones|Jones]] riguardo al fatto di assumere il comando dal compagno di bordo; ma.

Il progetto, essendo stato accolto con freddezza, lo aveva scoraggiato.

Non approfondire ulteriormente la questione, né dire nulla al riguardo

Il cuoco. Per coincidenza, era davvero molto prudente.

Nel pomeriggio, il cuoco esprimeva la sua determinazione…

Schierandosi dalla parte del compagno, si unì formalmente a quel gruppo; mentre…

[[characters/jones|Jones]] approfittò dell’occasione per litigare con Peters e fece delle allusioni.

Che avrebbe informato il compagno di bordo del piano in corso di attuazione.

Ora, evidentemente, non c’era più tempo da perdere, e Peters esprimeva il suo.

Determinazione a tentare di prendere la nave a tutti i costi.

“Se solo Augusto fosse disposto ad aiutarlo… Mio amico, immediatamente…”

Gli assicurò la propria disponibilità ad aderire a qualsiasi piano fosse stato proposto al riguardo.

Scopo e opportunità

Conosceva il fatto che fossi a bordo… A quel punto, quell’essere ibrido non fece nulla.

Più sorpreso che felice, poiché non aveva alcuna fiducia in quella situazione.

Su [[characters/jones|Jones]], che ormai considerava parte del loro gruppo.

Titolo:  
Del compagno di viaggio… Si recarono immediatamente sottocoperta, quando Augustus li chiamò.

Ci conoscemmo rapidamente; io e Peters diventammo subito amici.

Fu concordato che avremmo dovuto tentare di riprendere il velivolo.

La prima buona opportunità, lasciando completamente [[characters/jones|Jones]] fuori dalla nostra considerazione.

Consigli. In caso di [[success|successo]], avremmo dovuto dirigere la brigata verso.

Il primo porto che si offrì di accoglierla… La sua abbandono.

Il piano di Peters fallì a causa del suo gruppo

Un’avventura nel Pacifico che non avrebbe potuto essere realizzata senza…

L’equipaggio… e contava sul fatto di essere assolto al processo.

Titolo:  
Sulla questione della follia… (che egli ammise solennemente essere stata la motivazione delle sue azioni)

Titolo:  
(Nel momento in cui gli ha prestato aiuto per la rivolta, o dopo aver ottenuto qualcosa…)

Scusa, se dichiarato colpevole, a causa delle rappresentazioni di Augusto…

E io. Le nostre discussioni sono state momentaneamente interrotte…

Il grido “Tutti ai remi!”, e Peters con Augustus corsero subito.

Sul ponte.



Come al solito, l’equipaggio era quasi completamente ubriaco; e prima ancora che potessero salpare…

Una tempesta violenta gettò la brigata su un banco di sabbia

Beam-Ends… Ma tenendola lontana, riuscì comunque a rimettersi in sesto.

Fu spedita una grande quantità di [[motifs/water|acqua]]. Appena tutto fu sistemato in modo sicuro.

Quando un’altra tempesta colpì la nave, e subito dopo…

Un altro tentativo… senza danni causati. Sembrava proprio che…

Una tempesta di [[motifs/wind|vento]], che infatti poco dopo scoppiò con grande violenza.

Dai lati nord e ovest… Tutto era stato reso il più confortevole possibile.

Titolo:  
“Possibile… e come al solito ci mettemmo all’opera, sotto una vela ben tesa.”

Vela di prua. Con l'avanzare della [[motifs/night|notte]], il [[motifs/wind|vento]] divenne sempre più violento.

Titolo:  
Un mare straordinariamente agitato… Peters entrò ora nella plancia di comando.

Augusto, e riprendemmo le nostre deliberazioni.



Abbiamo concordato che nessuna opportunità potesse essere più vantaggiosa di questa.

Presente per realizzare i nostri progetti, come un tentativo di…

Un momento del genere non avrebbe mai potuto essere previsto… Mentre la brigata era al sicuro…

Pronta per l’uso, non ci sarebbe alcuna necessità di manovrarla fino a quando…

Buon tempo… se riuscissimo nel nostro tentativo, forse potremmo…

“Liberate uno, o forse due, di quegli uomini per aiutarci a prenderla.”

“In port. La principale difficoltà risiedeva nella grande disparità tra le nostre risorse…”

Solo in tre… e nella cabina…

Titolo:  
“Nove… Tutte le armi a bordo erano anche in loro possesso.”

Titolo:  
L’eccezione rappresentata da una coppia di piccole pistole che possedeva Peters

Nascosto addosso a lui, e il grande coltello da marina che portava con sé…

Sempre lo portava nella cintura dei suoi pantaloni… Da certi momenti…

Indicazioni, anche… come ad esempio il fatto che una cosa del genere semplicemente non esista.

Come un’ascia o una lancia appoggiate nei loro soliti posti… abbiamo iniziato.

Con la paura che il compagno potesse sospettare di qualcosa, almeno riguardo a.

Titolo:  
Peters… e che non avrebbe perso alcuna opportunità per sbarazzarsene.

Di lui. Era chiaro, davvero, che ciò che dovevamo decidere di fare…

Non si poteva aspettare altro che questo… Eppure le probabilità erano comunque troppo scarse contro di noi.

Ciò ci costringerebbe ad agire senza la massima cautela.



Peters suggerì di salire sul ponte e di entrare…

Conversazione con l’orologio (Allen): quando potrà farlo…

Get rid of him easily, senza alcun problema…

Disturbo… approfittando di un’ottima opportunità, quell’Augusto e…

“Allora dovrei intervenire io stesso e cercare di fornire ciò di cui abbiamo bisogno.”

Con qualche tipo di arma disponibile a bordo… e allora dovremmo…

Affrettiamoci tutti insieme e assicuriamo il passaggio di collegamento prima che sia troppo tardi.

Si poteva opporsi… Ma io mi sono opposto, perché non era giusto.

Non si può credere che quel tipo… un individuo davvero astuto, insomma…

Cose che non influenzavano i suoi pregiudizi superstiziosi

Non si può permettere di essere così facilmente ingannati… Il semplice fatto che ciò accada già rappresenta un problema grave.

Essere di guardia sul ponte era già una prova sufficiente del fatto che lui…

All’erta… – tranne che nei velivoli, dove è normale.

La disciplina viene applicata con la massima rigidezza, al punto di far montare sentinelle sul ponte.



<span class="atom-split" data-atom="chapter_07--part_02" data-title="The Narrative of A. Gordon Pym (Raven Edition) — Chapter 7 (part 2)" data-chapter="Chapter 07" data-kind="excerpt" data-tags="topos/double,motif/nature,motif/storm,motif/water,motif/well,motif/wind,concept/conscience,concept/doubt,concept/mercy,concept/nature"></span>


when a vessel is lying-to in a gale of [[motifs/wind|wind]]. As I address myself

principally, if not altogether, to persons who have never been to

sea, it may be as [[motifs/well|well]] to state the exact condition of a vessel

under such circumstances. Lying-to, or, in sea-parlance,

“laying-to,” is a measure resorted to for various purposes, and

effected in various manners. In moderate weather it is frequently

done with a view of merely bringing the vessel to a stand-still,

to wait for another vessel or any similar object. If the vessel

which lies-to is under full sail, the manoeuvre is usually

accomplished by throwing round some portion of her sails, so as

to let the [[motifs/wind|wind]] take them aback, when she becomes stationary. But

we are now speaking of lying-to in a gale of [[motifs/wind|wind]]. This is done

when the [[motifs/wind|wind]] is ahead, and too violent to admit of carrying sail

without danger of capsizing; and sometimes even when the [[motifs/wind|wind]] is

fair, but the sea too heavy for the vessel to be put before it.

If a vessel be suffered to scud before the [[motifs/wind|wind]] in a very heavy

sea, much damage is usually done her by the shipping of [[motifs/water|water]]

over her stern, and sometimes by the violent plunges she makes

forward. This manoeuvre, then, is seldom resorted to in such

case, unless through necessity. When the vessel is in a leaky

condition she is often put before the [[motifs/wind|wind]] even in the heaviest

seas; for, when lying-to, her seams are sure to be greatly opened

by her violent straining, and it is not so much the case when

scudding. Often, too, it becomes necessary to scud a vessel,

either when the blast is so exceedingly furious as to tear in

pieces the sail which is employed with a view of bringing her

head to the [[motifs/wind|wind]], or when, through the false modelling of the

frame or other causes, this main object cannot be effected.



Vessels in a gale of [[motifs/wind|wind]] are laid-to in different manners,

according to their peculiar construction. Some lie-to best under

a foresail, and this, I believe, is the sail most usually

employed. Large square-rigged vessels have sails for the express

purpose, called [[motifs/storm|storm]]-staysails. But the jib is occasionally

employed by itself,—sometimes the jib and foresail, or a

[[topoi/double|double]]-reefed foresail, and not unfrequently the after-sails, are

made use of. Foretopsails are very often found to answer the

purpose better than any other species of sail. The Grampus was

generally laid-to under a close-reefed foresail.



When a vessel is to be laid-to, her head is brought up to the

[[motifs/wind|wind]] just so nearly as to fill the sail under which she lies when

hauled flat aft, that is, when brought diagonally across the

vessel. This being done, the bows point within a few degrees of

the direction from which the [[motifs/wind|wind]] issues, and the windward bow of

course receives the shock of the waves. In this situation a good

vessel will ride out a very heavy gale of [[motifs/wind|wind]] without shipping a

drop of [[motifs/water|water]], and without any further attention being requisite

on the part of the crew. The helm is usually lashed down, but

this is altogether unnecessary (except on account of the noise it

makes when loose), for the rudder has no effect upon the vessel

when lying-to. Indeed, the helm had far better be left loose than

lashed very fast, for the rudder is apt to be torn off by heavy

seas if there be no room for the helm to play. As long as the

sail holds, a [[motifs/well|well]] modelled vessel will maintain her situation,

and ride every sea, as if instinct with life and reason. If the

violence of the [[motifs/wind|wind]], however, should tear the sail into pieces

(a feat which it requires a perfect hurricane to accomplish under

ordinary circumstances), there is then imminent danger. The

vessel falls off from the [[motifs/wind|wind]], and, coming broadside to the sea,

is completely at its [[concepts/mercy|mercy]]: the only resource in this case is to

put her quietly before the [[motifs/wind|wind]], letting her scud until some

other sail can be set. Some vessels will lie-to under no sail

whatever, but such are not to be trusted at sea.



But to return from this digression. It had never been customary

with the mate to have any watch on deck when lying-to in a gale

of [[motifs/wind|wind]], and the fact that he had now one, coupled with the

circumstance of the missing axes and handspikes, fully convinced

us that the crew were too [[motifs/well|well]] on the watch to be taken by

surprise in the manner Peters had suggested. Something, however,

was to be done, and that with as little delay as practicable, for

there could be no [[concepts/doubt|doubt]] that a suspicion having been once

entertained against Peters, he would be sacrificed upon the

earliest occasion, and one would certainly be either found or

made upon the breaking of the gale.



Augustus now suggested that if Peters could contrive to remove,

under any pretext, the piece of chain-cable which lay over the

trap in the stateroom, we might possibly be able to come upon

them unawares by means of the hold; but a little reflection

convinced us that the vessel rolled and pitched too violently for

any attempt of that [[concepts/nature|nature]].



By good fortune I at length hit upon the idea of working upon the

superstitious terrors and guilty [[concepts/conscience|conscience]] of the mate. It will

be remembered that one of the crew, Hartman Rogers, had died

during the morning, having been attacked two days before with

<span class="atom-split" data-atom="chapter_07--part_03" data-title="The Narrative of A. Gordon Pym (Raven Edition) — Chapter 7 (part 3)" data-chapter="Chapter 07" data-kind="excerpt" data-tags="archetype/villain,motif/blood,motif/chalk,motif/death,motif/noon,motif/time,motif/water,motif/well,concept/body"></span>


spasms after drinking some spirits and [[motifs/water|water]]. Peters had

expressed to us his opinion that this man had been poisoned by

the mate, and for this belief he had reasons, so he said, which

were incontrovertible, but which he could not be prevailed upon

to explain to us—this wayward refusal being only in keeping with

other points of his singular character. But whether or not he had

any better grounds for suspecting the mate than we had ourselves,

we were easily led to fall in with his suspicion, and determined

to act accordingly.



Rogers had died about eleven in the forenoon, in violent

convulsions; and the corpse presented in a few minutes after

[[motifs/death|death]] one of the most horrid and loathsome spectacles I ever

remember to have seen. The stomach was swollen immensely, like

that of a man who has been drowned and lain under [[motifs/water|water]] for many

weeks. The hands were in the same condition, while the face was

shrunken, shrivelled, and of a chalky whiteness, except where

relieved by two or three glaring red blotches like those

occasioned by the erysipelas: one of these blotches extended

diagonally across the face, completely covering up an eye as if

with a band of red velvet. In this disgusting condition the [[concepts/body|body]]

had been brought up from the cabin at [[motifs/noon|noon]] to be thrown

overboard, when the mate getting a glimpse of it (for he now saw

it for the first [[motifs/time|time]]), and being either touched with remorse for

his crime or struck with terror at so horrible a sight, ordered

the men to sew the [[concepts/body|body]] up in its hammock, and allow it the usual

rites of sea-burial. Having given these directions, he went

below, as if to avoid any further sight of his victim. While

preparations were making to obey his orders, the gale came on

with great fury, and the design was abandoned for the present.

The corpse, left to itself, was washed into the larboard

scuppers, where it still lay at the [[motifs/time|time]] of which I speak,

floundering about with the furious lurches of the brig.



Having arranged our plan, we set about putting it in execution as

speedily as possible. Peters went upon deck, and, as he had

anticipated, was immediately accosted by Allen, who appeared to

be stationed more as a watch upon the forecastle than for any

other purpose. The fate of this [[archetypes/villain|villain]], however, was speedily

and silently decided; for Peters, approaching him in a careless

manner, as if about to address him, seized him by the throat,

and, before he could utter a single cry, tossed him over the

bulwarks. He then called to us, and we came up. Our first

precaution was to look about for something with which to arm

ourselves, and in doing this we had to proceed with great care,

for it was impossible to stand on deck an instant without holding

fast, and violent seas broke over the vessel at every plunge

forward. It was indispensable, too, that we should be quick in

our operations, for every minute we expected the mate to be up to

set the pumps going, as it was evident the brig must be taking in

[[motifs/water|water]] very fast. After searching about for some [[motifs/time|time]], we could

find nothing more fit for our purpose than the two pump-handles,

one of which Augustus took, and I the other. Having secured

these, we stripped off the shirt of the corpse and dropped the

[[concepts/body|body]] overboard. Peters and myself then went below, leaving

Augustus to watch upon deck, where he took his station just where

Allen had been placed, and with his back to the cabin

companionway, so that, if any of the mate's gang should come up,

he might suppose it was the watch.



As soon as I got below I commenced disguising myself so as to

represent the corpse of Rogers. The shirt which we had taken from

the [[concepts/body|body]] aided us very much, for it was of singular form and

character, and easily recognizable—a kind of smock, which the

deceased wore over his other clothing. It was a blue stockinett,

with large white stripes running across. Having put this on, I

proceeded to equip myself with a false stomach, in [[Imitation|imitation]] of

the horrible deformity of the swollen corpse. This was soon

effected by means of stuffing with some bedclothes. I then gave

the same appearance to my hands by drawing on a pair of white

woollen mittens, and filling them in with any kind of rags that

offered themselves. Peters then arranged my face, first rubbing

it [[motifs/well|well]] over with white [[motifs/chalk|chalk]], and afterward blotching it with

[[motifs/blood|blood]], which he took from a cut in his finger. The streak across

the eye was not forgotten and presented a most shocking

appearance.

<span class="atom-split" data-atom="chapter_08--part_01" data-title="The Narrative of A. Gordon Pym (Raven Edition) — Chapter 8 (part 1)" data-chapter="Chapter 08" data-kind="excerpt" data-tags="motif/time,motif/well,motif/wind,form/fragment,character/jones"></span>


CHAPTER 8





As I viewed myself in a [[forms/fragment|fragment]] of looking-glass which hung up

in the cabin, and by the dim light of a kind of battle-lantern, I

was so impressed with a sense of vague awe at my appearance, and

at the recollection of the terrific reality which I was thus

representing, that I was seized with a violent tremour, and could

scarcely summon resolution to go on with my part. It was

necessary, however, to act with decision, and Peters and myself

went upon deck.



We there found everything safe, and, keeping close to the

bulwarks, the three of us crept to the cabin companion-way. It

was only partially closed, precautions having been taken to

prevent its being suddenly pushed to from without, by means of

placing billets of wood on the upper step so as to interfere with

the shutting. We found no difficulty in getting a full view of

the interior of the cabin through the cracks where the hinges

were placed. It now proved to have been very fortunate for us

that we had not attempted to take them by surprise, for they were

evidently on the alert. Only one was asleep, and he lying just at

the foot of the companion-ladder, with a musket by his side. The

rest were seated on several mattresses, which had been taken from

the berths and thrown on the floor. They were engaged in earnest

conversation; and although they had been carousing, as appeared

from two empty jugs, with some tin tumblers which lay about, they

were not as much intoxicated as usual. All had knives, one or two

of them pistols, and a great many muskets were lying in a berth

close at hand.



We listened to their conversation for some [[motifs/time|time]] before we could

make up our minds how to act, having as yet resolved on nothing

determinate, except that we would attempt to paralyze their

exertions, when we should attack them, by means of the apparition

of Rogers. They were discussing their piratical plans, in which

all we could hear distinctly was, that they would unite with the

crew of a schooner _Hornet_, and, if possible, get the schooner

herself into their possession preparatory to some attempt on a

large scale, the particulars of which could not be made out by

either of us.



One of the men spoke of Peters, when the mate replied to him in a

low voice which could not be distinguished, and afterward added

more loudly, that “he could not understand his being so much

forward with the captain’s brat in the forecastle, and he thought

the sooner both of them were overboard the better.” To this no

answer was made, but we could easily perceive that the hint was

[[motifs/well|well]] received by the whole party, and more particularly by [[characters/jones|Jones]].

At this period I was excessively agitated, the more so as I could

see that neither Augustus nor Peters could determine how to act.

I made up my mind, however, to sell my life as dearly as

possible, and not to suffer myself to be overcome by any feelings

of trepidation.



The tremendous noise made by the roaring of the [[motifs/wind|wind]] in the

rigging, and the washing of the sea over the deck, prevented us

from hearing what was said, except during momentary lulls. In one

of these, we all distinctly heard the mate tell one of the men to

“go forward, have an eye upon them, for he wanted no such secret

doings on board the brig.” It was [[motifs/well|well]] for us that the pitching

of the vessel at this moment was so violent as to prevent this

order from being carried into instant execution. The cook got up

from his mattress to go for us, when a tremendous lurch, which I

thought would carry away the masts, threw him headlong against

one of the larboard stateroom doors, bursting it open, and

creating a good deal of other confusion. Luckily, neither of our

party was thrown from his position, and we had [[motifs/time|time]] to make a

precipitate retreat to the forecastle, and arrange a hurried plan

of action before the messenger made his appearance, or rather

before he put his head out of the companion-hatch, for he did not

come on deck. From this station he could not notice the absence

of Allen, and he accordingly bawled out, as if to him, repeating

the orders of the mate. Peters cried out, “Ay, ay,” in a

disguised voice, and the cook immediately went below, without

entertaining a suspicion that all was not right.



My two companions now proceeded boldly aft and down into the

cabin, Peters closing the door after him in the same manner he

had found it. The mate received them with feigned cordiality, and

told Augustus that, since he had behaved himself so [[motifs/well|well]] of late,

he might take up his quarters in the cabin and be one of them for

the future. He then poured him out a tumbler half full of rum,

and made him drink it. All this I saw and heard, for I followed

my friends to the cabin as soon as the door was shut, and took up

my old point of observation. I had brought with me the two

pump-handles, one of which I secured near the companion-way, to

be ready for use when required.



I now steadied myself as [[motifs/well|well]] as possible so as to have a good

view of all that was passing within, and endeavoured to nerve

myself to the task of descending among the mutineers when Peters

should make a signal to me, as agreed upon. Presently he

contrived to turn the conversation upon the bloody deeds of the

mutiny, and by degrees led the men to talk of the thousand

superstitions which are so universally current among seamen. I


<span class="qlang-split" data-lang="it"></span>

CAPITOLO 8





Mentre mi guardavo in un [[forms/fragment|frammento]] di specchio appeso lì.

Nella cabina, alla luce fioca di una sorta di lanterna da battaglia, io…

Era così colpito da un vago senso di ammirazione per il mio aspetto…

Alla memoria di quella terribile realtà che così mi fu rivelata

Titolo:  
Rappresento che fui colto da un violento tremito e non riuscivo…

A malapena riesco a trovare la forza di continuare con il mio compito…

"Necessario, tuttavia, agire con decisione… Peters ed io."

Salì sul ponte.



Lì trovammo che tutto era al sicuro, e proseguimmo tenendoci vicini…

“Bulwarks: noi tre ci avvicinammo furtivamente al passaggio che conduceva alla cabina.”

Il titolo era solo parzialmente chiuso; erano state adottate alcune misure precauzionali.

Impedire che venga improvvisamente spinto dall’esterno

Titolo:  
Posizionare assi di legno sul gradino superiore al fine di ostacolarne l’uso…

La chiusura. Non abbiamo avuto alcuna difficoltà nel goderci una vista completa…

L’interno della cabina attraverso le fessure delle giunzioni

Fu una grande fortuna per noi.

Non avevamo tentato di coglierli di sorpresa, perché erano…

Chiaramente all’erta… Solo uno dormiva, e giaceva proprio lì.

“Alla base della scala di corda, con un fucile al suo fianco.”

Il resto delle persone era seduto su diversi materassi, che erano stati presi da…

“Il letto era sfatto e i vestiti gettati per terra; erano immersi nella loro attività con grande impegno.”

Conversazione… e sebbene avessero fatto baldoria, come sembrava…

Dai due secchi vuoti, insieme a alcuni bicchieri di latta che erano lì intorno, loro…

Non erano altrettanto ubriachi come al solito… Tutti avevano dei coltelli, uno o due per ciascuno.

“Tra di esse c’erano pistole, e moltissimi fucili erano riposti in un angolo.”

A portata di mano.



Abbiamo ascoltato la loro conversazione per un po' di [[motifs/time|tempo]] prima di riuscire a.

Decidere quale sia la nostra linea d’azione, visto che ancora non abbiamo preso alcuna decisione.

Titolo:  
Determinati… tranne che cercheremmo di paralizzarli.

"Sforzi che dovremmo attaccare, attraverso l’uso delle apparenzioni."

Di Rogers… Stavano discutendo i loro piani piratici.

L’unica cosa che riuscivamo a sentire chiaramente era che si sarebbero uniti…

Titolo:  
L’equipaggio della goletta “Hornet”… e, se possibile, prendere la goletta stessa.

Si mette nelle loro mani in preparazione a qualche tentativo…

Titolo:  
Su larga scala, i dettagli dei quali non sono stati possibile individuare.

Qualsiasiuno di noi due.



Uno degli uomini parlò di Peters, e il compagno gli rispose in un certo modo…

Voce bassa che non era possibile distinguere, e poi aggiunse…

Più forte, perché “non riusciva a capire il motivo per cui fosse così…”

“Avanti con quel moccioso del capitano nella prua… e lui pensava…”

“Meglio se entrambi finissero in acqua il prima possibile…” A questo, nessuno rispose.

La risposta è stata data, ma era facile intuire che l’indizio fosse…

Ben accolto da tutta la compagnia, e in particolare da [[characters/jones|Jones]].

In quel periodo ero estremamente agitato, soprattutto perché non riuscivo…

Si vedeva che né Augusto né Peters riuscivano a decidere cosa fare.

Ho deciso comunque di vendere la mia vita al prezzo più alto possibile…

“Possibile… e non permetterò che alcun sentimento mi sopraffaccia.”

di trepidazione.



Il terribile rumore prodotto dal ruggito del [[motifs/wind|vento]] nel.

La manovrabilità ridotta, nonché l’acqua del mare che si riversava sul ponte, ci hanno creato delle difficoltà.

Dall’ascolto di ciò che veniva detto, ad eccezione di brevi pause… In uno di quei momenti…

Di questi, abbiamo tutti sentito chiaramente il compagno dire a uno degli uomini di…

“Procedi pure, tienili d’occhio… perché lui non voleva che ci fossero segreti del genere.”

Le attività che avvenivano a bordo della brigata. Fu davvero una fortuna per noi che il movimento ondulatorio non fosse eccessivo.

In questo momento, la forza delle onde era così intensa da impedire qualsiasi movimento del vascello.

Ordine che venisse eseguito immediatamente. Il cuoco si alzò.

Dall’imbottitura del suo materasso… per andare a cercarci, quando un terribile scossone… che io…

Il pensiero potrebbe spezzare gli alberi… lo gettò dritto contro di essi

“Una delle porte delle cabine a babordo si aprì con violenza…”

Creando ulteriore confusione… Fortunatamente, nessuno dei due di noi…

La festa fu organizzata dalla sua posizione, e noi abbiamo avuto [[motifs/time|tempo]] per prepararla.

Ritirata affrettata verso la prua, e predisposizione di un piano frettoloso

Prima ancora che il messaggero comparisse…

Prima ancora di mettere la testa fuori dall’oblò di comunicazione… perché non lo fece.

“Vieni su Deck… Da questa postazione non riusciva a notare la sua assenza.”

“Di Allen… e così gridò, come se si stesse rivolgendo a lui, ripetendo…”

“Gli ordini del secondo…”, gridò Peters, “Sì, sì!”

Voce camuffata… e il cuoco si precipitò immediatamente giù, senza indugio.

Era tormentato dal sospetto che qualcosa non andasse per il verso giusto.



I miei due compagni proseguirono coraggiosamente verso poppa e in basso…

Cabin: Peters chiude la porta dietro di sé nello stesso modo in cui…

Li aveva trovati. Il compagno li accolse con una falsa cordialità…

disse ad Augusto che, poiché si era comportato così [[motifs/well|benissimo]] negli ultimi tempi,

Potrebbe stabilirsi nella cabina e diventare uno di loro.

Il futuro… Poi gli versò un bicchiere mezzo pieno di rum.

E lo costrinsero a berlo. Tutto ciò che vidi e udii… perché li seguii.

Non appena la porta si chiuse, li portai tutti nella capanna e iniziammo…

Il mio vecchio punto di osservazione… Avevo portato con me quelle due cose.

Titolo:  
Le maniglie della pompa… una delle quali ho fissato vicino al passaggio laterale…

Essere pronto all’uso quando necessario.



Ora mi sono ripreso il più possibile, in modo da poter fare bene.

Visione di tutto ciò che avveniva all’interno, e si sforzava di trovare il coraggio necessario…

Mi addossai la responsabilità di scendere tra i ribelli, quando Peters…

“Dovrebbe inviarmi un segnale, come concordato. In questo momento…”

Riuscito a deviare la conversazione sui crimini sanguinosi di…

Mutino… e gradualmente portò gli uomini a parlare di quella “migliaia”.

Superstizioni ampiamente diffuse tra i marinai



<span class="atom-split" data-atom="chapter_08--part_02" data-title="The Narrative of A. Gordon Pym (Raven Edition) — Chapter 8 (part 2)" data-chapter="Chapter 08" data-kind="excerpt" data-tags="archetype/shadow,archetype/villain,motif/nature,motif/time,concept/body,concept/deception,concept/despair,concept/doubt,concept/hope,concept/nature,concept/suffering,concept/wonder,character/bottom,character/jones,character/richard"></span>


could not make out all that was said, but I could plainly see the

effects of the conversation in the countenances of those present.

The mate was evidently much agitated, and presently, when some

one mentioned the terrific appearance of Rogers’ corpse, I

thought he was upon the point of swooning. Peters now asked him

if he did not think it would be better to have the [[concepts/body|body]] thrown

overboard at once as it was too horrible a sight to see it

floundering about in the scuppers. At this the [[archetypes/villain|villain]] absolutely

gasped for breath, and turned his head slowly round upon his

companions, as if imploring some one to go up and perform the

task. No one, however, stirred, and it was quite evident that the

whole party were wound up to the highest pitch of nervous

excitement. Peters now made me the signal. I immediately threw

open the door of the companion-way, and, descending, without

uttering a syllable, stood erect in the midst of the party.



The intense effect produced by this sudden apparition is not at

all to be wondered at when the various circumstances are taken

into consideration. Usually, in cases of a similar [[concepts/nature|nature]], there

is left in the mind of the spectator some glimmering of [[concepts/doubt|doubt]] as

to the reality of the vision before his eyes; a degree of [[concepts/hope|hope]],

however feeble, that he is the victim of chicanery, and that the

apparition is not actually a visitant from the old world of

shadows. It is not too much to say that such remnants of [[concepts/doubt|doubt]]

have been at the [[characters/bottom|bottom]] of almost every such visitation, and that

the appalling horror which has sometimes been brought about, is

to be attributed, even in the cases most in point, and where most

[[concepts/suffering|suffering]] has been experienced, more to a kind of anticipative

horror, lest the apparition might possibly be real, than to an

unwavering belief in its reality. But, in the present instance,

it will be seen immediately, that in the minds of the mutineers

there was not even the [[archetypes/shadow|shadow]] of a basis upon which to rest a

[[concepts/doubt|doubt]] that the apparition of Rogers was indeed a revivification

of his disgusting corpse, or at least its spiritual image. The

isolated situation of the brig, with its entire inaccessibility

on account of the gale, confined the apparently possible means of

[[concepts/deception|deception]] within such narrow and definite limits, that they must

have thought themselves enabled to survey them all at a glance.

They had now been at sea twenty-four days, without holding more

than a speaking communication with any vessel whatever. The whole

of the crew, too—at least all whom they had the most remote

reason for suspecting to be on board—were assembled in the cabin,

with the exception of Allen, the watch; and his gigantic stature

(he was six feet six inches high) was too familiar in their eyes

to permit the notion that he was the apparition before them to

enter their minds even for an instant. Add to these

considerations the awe-inspiring [[concepts/nature|nature]] of the tempest, and that

of the conversation brought about by Peters; the deep impression

which the loathsomeness of the actual corpse had made in the

morning upon the imaginations of the men; the excellence of the

[[Imitation|imitation]] in my person, and the uncertain and wavering light in

which they beheld me, as the glare of the cabin lantern, swinging

violently to and fro, fell dubiously and fitfully upon my figure,

and there will be no reason to [[concepts/wonder|wonder]] that the [[concepts/deception|deception]] had even

more than the entire effect which we had anticipated. The mate

sprang up from the mattress on which he was lying, and, without

uttering a syllable, fell back, stone dead, upon the cabin floor,

and was hurled to the leeward like a log by a heavy roll of the

brig. Of the remaining seven, there were but three who had at

first any degree of presence of mind. The four others sat for

some [[motifs/time|time]] rooted apparently to the floor, the most pitiable

objects of horror and utter [[concepts/despair|despair]] my eyes ever encountered. The

only opposition we experienced at all was from the cook, John

Hunt, and [[characters/richard|Richard]] Parker; but they made but a feeble and

irresolute defence. The two former were shot instantly by Peters,

and I felled Parker with a blow on the head from the pump-handle

which I had brought with me. In the meantime, Augustus seized one

of the muskets lying on the floor and shot another mutineer

Wilson through the breast. There were now but three remaining;

but by this [[motifs/time|time]] they had become aroused from their lethargy, and

perhaps began to see that a [[concepts/deception|deception]] had been practised upon

them, for they fought with great resolution and fury, and, but

for the immense muscular strength of Peters, might have

ultimately got the better of us. These three men were—[[characters/jones|Jones]],

Greely, and Absolom Hicks. [[characters/jones|Jones]] had thrown Augustus to the

floor, stabbed him in several places along the right arm, and

would no [[concepts/doubt|doubt]] have soon dispatched him (as neither Peters nor

myself could immediately get rid of our own antagonists), had it

not been for the timely aid of a friend, upon whose assistance

we, surely, had never depended. This friend was no other than

Tiger. With a low growl, he bounded into the cabin, at a most

critical moment for Augustus, and throwing himself upon [[characters/jones|Jones]],

pinned him to the floor in an instant. My friend, however, was

now too much injured to render us any aid whatever, and I was so


<span class="qlang-split" data-lang="it"></span>

Non riuscivo a capire tutto ciò che veniva detto, ma vedevo chiaramente…

Gli effetti della conversazione si riflettevano sui volti delle persone presenti.

Il compagno era evidentemente molto agitato, e presto, quando qualcuno…

Uno ha menzionato l’aspetto terribile del cadavere di Rogers…

Titolo:  
Peters pensò che stesse per svenire. Allora gli chiese…

Se non pensava che fosse meglio gettare via il [[concepts/body|corpo]].

Gettato immediatamente in mare, perché la scena era troppo orribile da sopportare

Barcollando nel rigoglioso giardino. A questo punto, il [[archetypes/villain|villano]] fu completamente.

Trattenendo il respiro, girò lentamente la testa verso di lui…

Compagni, come se implorassero qualcuno di salire e eseguire…

Titolo:  
Nessuno si mosse; era evidente che…

Tutta la compagnia era tesa al massimo grado di nervosismo.

Emozione… Peters mi fece subito il segnale; immediatamente reagii.

Aprire la porta del passaggio laterale e scendere, senza…

Mentre pronunciava una sillaba, si alzò dritto in piedi nel mezzo del gruppo.



L’intenso effetto prodotto da questa improvvisa apparizione non è affatto…

Tutto merita meraviglia quando si considerano tutte le circostanze.

Vanno presi in considerazione. Di solito, in casi di simile [[concepts/nature|natura]], ci.

Resta nella mente dello spettatore un barlume di [[concepts/doubt|dubbio]], come.

di fronte alla realtà di quella visione davanti ai suoi occhi, un certo grado di [[concepts/hope|speranza]].

Qualunque sia la sua debolezza, è vittima di truffe… e questo…

“Apparizione non è in realtà un visitatore dal vecchio mondo…”

Ombre. Non è esagerato dire che tali rimanenti di [[concepts/doubt|dubbio]].

Sono sempre stato al [[characters/bottom|fondo]] di quasi ogni visita del genere, e questo è vero.

L’orribile orrore che a volte si è verificato…

Titolo:  
Da attribuire, anche nei casi più rilevanti e dove ciò sia maggiormente opportuno…

Il [[concepts/suffering|soffrire]] è stato vissuto, in un certo senso come una sorta di attesa anticipata.

Terrore… nel timore che quell’apparizione potesse essere reale.

Fede incrollabile nella sua realtà… Ma, nel caso attuale,

Come si potrà immediatamente notare, nella mente dei ribelli…

Non c'era nemmeno l'[[archetypes/shadow|ombra]] di una base su cui poter fare affidamento.

[[concepts/doubt|Dubito]] che l'apparizione di Rogers fosse davvero un ritorno in vita.

Di quel suo cadavere disgustoso, o almeno della sua immagine spirituale.

Situazione isolata della brigata, con la sua totale inaccessibilità

A causa della tempesta, i mezzi apparentemente disponibili per… sono stati limitati.

La [[concepts/deception|inganno]] è confinata entro limiti così stretti e precisi, che deve necessariamente.

Hanno pensato di poterli esaminare tutti in un solo sguardo.

Erano ormai in mare da ventiquattro giorni, senza aver fatto altre soste.

Più efficace di qualsiasi forma di comunicazione verbale con qualsiasi nave esista… Il tutto.

Di tutto l’equipaggio, almeno di coloro che erano loro più vicini…

Riuniti nella cabina…

“Ad eccezione di Allen… l’orologio… e la sua imponente statura.”

“Era alto sei piedi e sei pollici”… una figura troppo familiare ai loro occhi.

Permettere l’idea che fosse proprio lui quell’apparizione davanti a loro…

Non entrano nemmeno per un istante nelle loro menti. Aggiungi a questo…

Considerando la maestosa [[concepts/nature|natura]] della tempesta, e anche il resto.

Il dialogo scaturito dalle parole di Peters; l’impressione profonda che ne è risultata

Titolo:  
La ripugnanza del cadavere reale aveva reso…

“Alba nelle immaginazioni degli uomini: l’eccellenza…”

Un’[[Imitation|imitazione]] di me stesso, e quella luce incerta e vacillante.

Che mi vedessero, alla luce tremolante della lanterna nella cabina…

Con violenza e incertezza, cadeva ripetutamente sulla mia figura.

E non ci sarà alcun motivo per [[concepts/wonder|meravigliarsi]] del fatto che quella [[concepts/deception|inganno]] sia mai avvenuta.

Un effetto molto più grande di quanto avessimo previsto… Il compagno

Saltò fuori dal materasso su cui era sdraiato, e… senza indugio.

Cadde a terra, privo di vita, sul pavimento della capanna…

E fu scagliato verso poppa come un tronco, a causa di una forte ondata…

Titolo:  
Dei sette rimanenti, solo tre erano ancora disponibili…

Nessuna presenza di spirito. Gli altri quattro rimasero seduti…

A volte, sembrava radicato per sempre nel terreno, il più misero di tutti.

Oggetti di orrore e segni di totale [[concepts/despair|-disperazione]], mai visti prima dai miei occhi.

L’unica opposizione che abbiamo incontrato è stata da parte del cuoco, John.

Hunt e [[characters/richard|Richard]] Parker, ma i loro sforzi risultarono deboli e inefficaci.

"Difesa indecisa. I primi due furono uccisi all’istante da Peters."

E con un colpo alla testa, usando il manico della pompa, ho abbattuto Parker

Quello che avevo portato con me… Nel frattempo, Augusto ne prese uno.

Dei fucili posati a terra e di un altro ammutinato che venne ucciso

Wilson, colpito al petto… Ora ne rimanevano soltanto tre.

Ma a quel [[motifs/time|momento]] erano già usciti dal loro letargo, e.

Forse iniziò a rendersi conto che qualcuno aveva commesso una [[concepts/deception|inganno]] nei suoi confronti.

Loro, perché combatterono con grande determinazione e furia…

Con la straordinaria forza muscolare di Peters, avrebbe potuto...

Alla fine riuscì a batterci. Questi tre uomini erano. [[characters/jones|Jones]],

Greely, e Absolom Hicks. [[characters/jones|Jones]] aveva gettato Augustus.

Gli ha pugnalato diverse volte il braccio destro

Non avrei certo [[concepts/doubt|dubitato]] che lo avrebbero presto eliminato (poiché né Peters né, ).

Potrei liberarmi immediatamente dei nostri stessi avversari, se solo…

Se non fosse stato per l’aiuto tempestivo di un amico, il cui intervento è stato decisivo…

Certamente, non ci eravamo mai affidati a nessuno… Questo amico non era altri che…

Tigre… Con un ruggito sommesso, irruppe nella cabina, con grande velocità.

Un momento critico per Augustus, che si gettò su [[characters/jones|Jones]].

Lo inchiodò a terra in un istante… Mio amico, invece, riuscì a…

Ora è troppo ferito per poterci essere di alcun aiuto… E io ero così…



<span class="atom-split" data-atom="chapter_08--part_03" data-title="The Narrative of A. Gordon Pym (Raven Edition) — Chapter 8 (part 3)" data-chapter="Chapter 08" data-kind="excerpt" data-tags="motif/blood,motif/clock,motif/crown,motif/night,motif/ship,motif/time,motif/water,motif/well,motif/wind,concept/doubt,concept/mercy,setting/ship,character/jones,character/richard"></span>


encumbered with my disguise that I could do but little. The dog

would not leave his hold upon the throat of [[characters/jones|Jones]]—Peters,

nevertheless, was far more than a match for the two men who

remained, and would, no [[concepts/doubt|doubt]], have dispatched them sooner, had

it not been for the narrow space in which he had to act, and the

tremendous lurches of the vessel. Presently he was enabled to get

hold of a heavy stool, several of which lay about the floor. With

this he beat out the brains of Greely as he was in the act of

discharging a musket at me, and immediately afterward a roll of

the brig throwing him in contact with Hicks, he seized him by the

throat, and, by dint of sheer strength, strangled him

instantaneously. Thus, in far less [[motifs/time|time]] than I have taken to tell

it, we found ourselves masters of the brig.



The only person of our opponents who was left alive was [[characters/richard|Richard]]

Parker. This man, it will be remembered, I had knocked down with

a blow from the pump-handle at the commencement of the attack. He

now lay motionless by the door of the shattered stateroom; but,

upon Peters touching him with his foot, he spoke, and entreated

for [[concepts/mercy|mercy]]. His head was only slightly cut, and otherwise he had

received no injury, having been merely stunned by the blow. He

now got up, and, for the present, we secured his hands behind his

back. The dog was still growling over [[characters/jones|Jones]]; but, upon

examination, we found him completely dead, the [[motifs/blood|blood]] issuing in a

stream from a deep wound in the throat, inflicted, no [[concepts/doubt|doubt]], by

the sharp teeth of the animal.



It was now about one o’[[motifs/clock|clock]] in the morning, and the [[motifs/wind|wind]] was

still blowing tremendously. The brig evidently laboured much more

than usual, and it became absolutely necessary that something

should be done with a view of easing her in some measure. At

almost every roll to leeward she shipped a sea, several of which

came partially down into the cabin during our scuffle, the

hatchway having been left open by myself when I descended. The

entire range of bulwarks to larboard had been swept away, as [[motifs/well|well]]

as the caboose, together with the jollyboat from the counter. The

creaking and working of the mainmast, too, gave indication that

it was nearly sprung. To make room for more stowage in the

afterhold, the heel of this mast had been stepped between decks

(a very reprehensible practice, occasionally resorted to by

ignorant [[motifs/ship|ship]]-builders), so that it was in imminent danger of

working from its step. But, to [[motifs/crown|crown]] all our difficulties, we

plummed the [[motifs/well|well]], and found no less than seven feet of [[motifs/water|water]].



Leaving the bodies of the crew lying in the cabin, we got to work

immediately at the pumps—Parker, of course, being set at liberty

to assist us in the labour. Augustus’s arm was bound up as [[motifs/well|well]]

as we could effect it, and he did what he could, but that was not

much. However, we found that we could just manage to keep the

leak from gaining upon us by having one pump constantly going. As

there were only four of us, this was severe labour; but we

endeavoured to keep up our spirits, and looked anxiously for

daybreak, when we hoped to lighten the brig by cutting away the

mainmast.



In this manner we passed a [[motifs/night|night]] of terrible anxiety and fatigue,

and, when the day at length broke, the gale had neither abated in

the least, nor were there any signs of its abating. We now

dragged the bodies on deck and threw them overboard. Our next

care was to get rid of the mainmast. The necessary preparations

having been made, Peters cut away at the mast (having found axes

in the cabin), while the rest of us stood by the stays and

lanyards. As the brig gave a tremendous lee-lurch, the word was

given to cut away the weather-lanyards, which being done, the

whole mass of wood and rigging plunged into the sea, clear of the

brig, and without doing any material injury. We now found that

the vessel did not labour quite as much as before, but our

situation was still exceedingly precarious, and in spite of the

utmost exertions, we could not gain upon the leak without the aid

of both pumps. The little assistance which Augustus could render

us was not really of any importance. To add to our distress, a

heavy sea, striking the brig to the windward, threw her off

several points from the [[motifs/wind|wind]], and, before she could regain her

position, another broke completely over her, and hurled her full

upon her beam-ends. The ballast now shifted in a mass to leeward

(the stowage had been knocking about perfectly at random for some

[[motifs/time|time]]), and for a few moments we thought nothing could save us

from capsizing. Presently, however, we partially righted; but the

ballast still retaining its place to larboard, we lay so much

along that it was useless to think of working the pumps, which

indeed we could not have done much longer in any case, as our

hands were entirely raw with the excessive labour we had

undergone, and were bleeding in the most horrible manner.



Contrary to Parker’s advice, we now proceeded to cut away the

foremast, and at length accomplished it after much difficulty,

owing to the position in which we lay. In going overboard the

wreck took with it the bowsprit, and left us a complete hulk.



So far we had had reason to rejoice in the escape of our

longboat, which had received no damage from any of the huge seas


<span class="qlang-split" data-lang="it"></span>

Con il mio travestimento addosso, non riuscivo a fare quasi nulla… Il cane.

Non avrebbe mai allentato la presa sulla gola di [[characters/jones|Jones]]—Peters.

Nonostante ciò, era di gran lunga all’altezza dei due uomini…

Rimase lì, e senza alcun [[concepts/doubt|dubbio]] li avrebbe inviati via prima, se solo.

Se non fosse stato per lo spazio ristretto entro cui doveva agire…

Terribili scossoni della nave… Alla fine riuscì a…

Tenendo in mano uno sgabello pesante, tra quelli sparsi per il pavimento…

Questo gli ha fatto perdere la ragione mentre stava compiendo quel gesto

Sparando un moschetto contro di me, e immediatamente dopo…

Il brig lo portò a contatto con Hicks; lui lo afferrò per…

Titolo:  
Gli strinse la gola e, con la sola forza bruta, lo soffocò

In modo istantaneo. Pertanto, in molto meno [[motifs/time|tempo]] di quanto ne abbia impiegato io per raccontarlo.

Così, ci trovammo padroni della nave brigantino.



L’unica persona dei nostri avversari che rimase viva fu [[characters/richard|Richard]].

Parker. Quest’uomo, come si ricorderà, lo avevo steso con…

Un colpo con il manico della pompa all’inizio dell’attacco… Lui.

Ora giace immobile accanto alla porta della cabina distrutta…

Quando Peters lo toccò con il piede, parlò e pregò.

Per [[concepts/mercy|migliozza]]. La sua testa era solo leggermente ferita; per il resto, stava bene.

Non ha riportato alcuna ferita, essendo stato soltanto stordito dal colpo. Lui

which had come on board. But we had not long to congratulate

foresail with it, by which the brig had been steadied, every sea

now made a complete breach over us, and in five minutes our deck

was swept from stem to stern, the longboat and starboard bulwarks

torn off, and even the windlass shattered into fragments. It was,

indeed, hardly possible for us to be in a more pitiable

condition.



At [[motifs/noon|noon]] there seemed to be some slight appearance of the gale’s

abating, but in this we were sadly disappointed, for it only

lulled for a few minutes to blow with redoubled fury. About four

in the afternoon it was utterly impossible to stand up against

the violence of the blast; and, as the [[motifs/night|night]] closed in upon us, I

had not a [[archetypes/shadow|shadow]] of [[concepts/hope|hope]] that the vessel would hold together

until morning.



By midnight we had settled very deep in the [[motifs/water|water]], which was now

up to the orlop deck. The rudder went soon afterward, the sea

which tore it away lifting the after portion of the brig entirely

from the [[motifs/water|water]], against which she thumped in her descent with

such a concussion as would be occasioned by going ashore. We had

all calculated that the rudder would hold its own to the last, as

it was unusually strong, being rigged as I have never seen one

rigged either before or since. Down its main timber there ran a

succession of stout iron hooks, and others in the same manner

down the stern-post. Through these hooks there extended a very

thick wrought-iron rod, the rudder being thus held to the

stern-post and swinging freely on the rod. The tremendous force

of the sea which tore it off may be estimated by the fact, that

the hooks in the stern-post, which ran entirely through it, being

clinched on the inside, were drawn every one of them completely

out of the solid wood.



We had scarcely [[motifs/time|time]] to draw breath after the violence of this

shock, when one of the most tremendous waves I had then ever

known broke right on board of us, sweeping the companion-way

clear off, bursting in the hatchways, and filling every inch of

the vessel with [[motifs/water|water]].

Gordon Pym (Raven Edition) — Chapter 9 (part 1)" data-chapter="Chapter 09" data-kind="excerpt" data-tags="motif/nature,motif/night,motif/pain,motif/silence,motif/time,motif/water,motif/wind,concept/body,concept/courage,concept/hope,concept/mercy,concept/nature"></span>


CHAPTER 9





Luckily, just before [[motifs/night|night]], all four of us had lashed ourselves

firmly to the fragments of the windlass, lying in this manner as

flat upon the deck as possible. This precaution [[Alone|alone]] saved us

from destruction. As it was, we were all more or less stunned by

the immense weight of [[motifs/water|water]] which tumbled upon us, and which did

not roll from above us until we were nearly exhausted. As soon as

I could recover breath, I called aloud to my companions. Augustus

[[Alone|alone]] replied, saying: “It is all over with us, and may God have

[[concepts/mercy|mercy]] upon our souls!” By-and-by both the others were enabled to

speak, when they exhorted us to take [[concepts/courage|courage]], as there was still

[[concepts/hope|hope]]; it being impossible, from the [[concepts/nature|nature]] of the cargo, that the

brig could go down, and there being every chance that the gale

would blow over by the morning. These words inspired me with new

life; for, strange as it may seem, although it was obvious that a

vessel with a cargo of empty oil-casks would not sink, I had been

hitherto so confused in mind as to have overlooked this

consideration altogether; and the danger which I had for some

[[motifs/time|time]] regarded as the most imminent was that of foundering. As

[[concepts/hope|hope]] revived within me, I made use of every opportunity to

strengthen the lashings which held me to the remains of the

windlass, and in this occupation I soon discovered that my

companions were also busy. The [[motifs/night|night]] was as dark as it could

possibly be, and the horrible shrieking din and confusion which

surrounded us it is useless to attempt describing. Our deck lay

level with the sea, or rather we were encircled with a towering

ridge of foam, a portion of which swept over us every instant. It

is not too much to say that our heads were not fairly out of the

[[motifs/water|water]] more than one second in three. Although we lay close

together, no one of us could see the other, or, indeed, any

portion of the brig itself, upon which we were so tempestuously

hurled about. At intervals we called one to the other, thus

endeavouring to keep alive [[concepts/hope|hope]], and render consolation and

encouragement to such of us as stood most in need of it. The

feeble condition of Augustus made him an object of solicitude

with us all; and as, from the lacerated condition of his right

arm, it must have been impossible for him to secure his lashings

with any degree of firmness, we were in momentary expectation of

finding that he had gone overboard—yet to render him aid was a

thing altogether out of the question. Fortunately, his station

was more secure than that of any of the rest of us; for the upper

part of his [[concepts/body|body]] lying just beneath a portion of the shattered

windlass, the seas, as they tumbled in upon him, were greatly

broken in their violence. In any other situation than this (into

which he had been accidentally thrown after having lashed himself

in a very exposed spot) he must inevitably have perished before

morning. Owing to the brig’s lying so much along, we were all

less liable to be washed off than otherwise would have been the

case. The heel, as I have before stated, was to larboard, about

one half of the deck being constantly under [[motifs/water|water]]. The seas,

therefore, which struck us to starboard were much broken, by the

vessel’s side, only reaching us in fragments as we lay flat on

our faces; while those which came from larboard being what are

called back-[[motifs/water|water]] seas, and obtaining little hold upon us on

account of our posture, had not sufficient force to drag us from

our fastenings.



In this frightful situation we lay until the day broke so as to

show us more fully the horrors which surrounded us. The brig was

a mere log, [[rolling]] about at the [[concepts/mercy|mercy]] of every wave; the gale

was upon the increase, if any thing, blowing indeed a complete

hurricane, and there appeared to us no earthly prospect of

deliverance. For several hours we held on in [[motifs/silence|silence]], expecting

every moment that our lashings would either give way, that the

remains of the windlass would go by the board, or that some of

the huge seas, which roared in every direction around us and

above us, would drive the hulk so far beneath the [[motifs/water|water]] that we

should be drowned before it could regain the surface. By the

[[concepts/mercy|mercy]] of God, however, we were preserved from these imminent

dangers, and about midday were cheered by the light of the

blessed sun. Shortly afterward we could perceive a sensible

diminution in the force of the [[motifs/wind|wind]], when, now for the first [[motifs/time|time]]

since the latter part of the evening before, Augustus spoke,

asking Peters, who lay closest to him, if he thought there was

any possibility of our being saved. As no reply was at first made

to this question, we all concluded that the hybrid had been

drowned where he lay; but presently, to our great joy, he spoke,

although very feebly, saying that he was in great [[motifs/pain|pain]], being so

cut by the tightness of his lashings across the stomach, that he

must either find means of loosening them or perish, as it was

impossible that he could endure his misery much longer. This

occasioned us great distress, as it was altogether useless to

think of aiding him in any manner while the sea continued washing

over us as it did. We exhorted him to bear his sufferings with

fortitude, and promised to seize the first opportunity which
